extra.reason: Implemented POST /print-pdf in commit 5b78f52 (CI run 30675560656 green). Takes the same {device, data} envelope as /write with data as a base64-encoded PDF; undecodable base64 and a missing %PDF signature are plain-text 400s, a body over 50 MB is 413, all before any CUPS call. Spools via cupsClient.printDocument WITHOUT -o raw so CUPS renders the PDF through its filter chain. Reuses resolveTarget for queue selection and USB-to-network failover and the new shared enforceOrigin for the --origin-allow gate, so the allowlist cannot be bypassed by posting a PDF instead of ZPL. Success is the same empty 200, failures the same plain-text bodies; CORS echo, X-Print-Agent-Version and OPTIONS preflight behave as on every other route including the new error paths. The five frozen routes and the Device shape are unchanged (discovery.go/identity.go/version.go/health.go untouched; all 14 pre-existing tests still pass). Four new Go tests wired to four new lat.md/tests.md sections; the no--o-raw invariant is asserted directly and negative-controlled. Documented in lat.md/tools.md (new Document Printing section), README.md (route marked additive) and RUNBOOK.md. NOT released: no tag, no release cut.

VERIFIED ON HARDWARE and closed. The station was upgraded to v0.2.1 (X-Print-Agent-Version and the pkgutil receipt both report 0.2.1) and the agent's own code was exercised, not a hand-typed lp command.

FLIPPING-DRIVER DIRECTION, verified end to end: a 4x5 PDF POSTed to /print-pdf printed RIGHT-SIDE UP on the Zebra ZD621, whose queue reports printer-make-and-model='Zebra ZPL Label Printer' — so detection fired and the counter-rotation landed the page upright against rastertolabel's unconditional ^POI. The same content sent through /write as ZPL with a pinned ^PON also printed right-side up. Both paths agree, which is what the acceptance asked for. Note they were confirmed in separate prints rather than one batch, for the reason below.

NON-FLIPPING DIRECTION, NOT hardware-verified and deliberately not claimed as such: the station has exactly one configured queue, so there is no non-flipping driver to test against without adding a queue to the owner's machine. That direction rests on TestPrintPDFLeavesANonInvertingDriverAlone, whose sharpest sub-case is a Zebra CPCL queue driven by the SAME rastertolabel binary that must not be rotated, plus a probe-failure sub-case pinning the safe default.

SEPARATE ANOMALY, not this bug, filed as its own bead: a PDF job and a ZPL job submitted back to back produced only ONE physical label even though CUPS marked both complete and the agent logged success for each. Sent alone immediately afterwards, the identical PDF printed correctly. So the PDF path is sound and the loss is in rapid successive submission — media advance, top-of-form, or job pacing.

METHOD NOTE for anyone re-testing: size the probe page to the queue's DefaultPageSize, w288h360 (4.00x5.00in). A 4x6 page blanks when rotated because the ink moves past the shorter label, which reads as a mechanism failure and nearly triggered an unnecessary redesign during this investigation.
